description: Trigger discrimination for designing how an AI feature's output becomes product state (D70, #285/#286 with #287) against the neighbors named in its description and the Phase 7 batch proposal: the coding assistant's own approvals (human-approval-boundary), what agents building the product may do (agent-authorization-matrix, manual-only), per-tool permission scope (agent-tool-safety-guard), the oversight level a risk tier needs (ai-governance-risk-reviewer), and adversarial review of an approval flow (human-agent-trust-reviewer).

cases.prompt: Our AI drafts changes to customer records. Design the approval step so a person reviews, edits or rejects each change before it is saved.
cases.reason: The product's review workflow for AI output is this skill; human-approval-boundary governs the coding assistant's own risky steps, and agent-tool-safety-guard scopes tools rather than designing the review.

cases.prompt: Before I run this migration that renames the billing columns in production, check whether I already have approval or need to ask the owner.
cases.reason: An imminent risky step by the coding assistant is human-approval-boundary; no product AI feature's workflow is being designed.

cases.prompt: Which things should our AI scheduling assistant be allowed to do by itself, which need the user to confirm, and which should it never do?
cases.reason: Sorting a product AI feature's actions into AUTONOMOUS, CONFIRM and FORBIDDEN is this skill's first step; agent-authorization-matrix covers agents building the product, and ai-governance-risk-reviewer sets the tier rather than classifying each action.

cases.prompt: Explicitly invoke agent-authorization-matrix. Define what our coding agents may merge, deploy or change in this repository without asking a person first.
cases.reason: Standing authority for the agents building the product is agent-authorization-matrix (manual-only, named explicitly); this skill designs a product AI feature's path to product state.

cases.prompt: Our support agent can call issue_refund and close_account. Scope each tool to least privilege, run it as the calling user and validate its arguments.
cases.reason: Per-tool permission scope, identity and argument validation are agent-tool-safety-guard; the review workflow an approval-gated call then goes through is this skill.

cases.prompt: Our agent's issue_refund tool is already marked as needing approval. Design the queue support leads use: what they see, approve or edit or reject, expiry, and the audit trail.
cases.reason: The tool gate exists; designing the review queue and decisions behind it is this skill, not tool permission scope.

cases.prompt: Our AI credit-limit advisor affects customers' finances. What risk tier is it, and does it need human in the loop or is human on the loop enough?
cases.reason: Setting the risk tier and the oversight level it requires is ai-governance-risk-reviewer; this skill consumes that decision and designs the workflow.

cases.prompt: The risk review says our AI invoice-coding feature must stay advisory-only. Design how its suggestions reach users without the AI writing anything.
cases.reason: The oversight level is decided; designing the advisory-only pattern that delivers it is this skill.

cases.prompt: Approvers click yes on almost every agent request within seconds. Attack our approval screen for consent fatigue, misleading summaries and bundled dangerous steps.
cases.reason: Adversarially reviewing an existing approval flow is human-agent-trust-reviewer; this skill designs the flow and hands it there for attack review.

cases.prompt: AI-suggested edits to a contract record sometimes get approved after someone else has already changed the record. How should the review flow handle that?
cases.reason: Proposal staleness and base-version checks before commit are part of the review workflow this skill designs; nothing here is an attack review or the coding assistant's own approval.
